source:
Roblox Grand Strategy Game Design

Game Overview

Create a multiplayer grand strategy game set on a fictional continent based on the land shape of Europe. The coastlines, mountains, rivers, islands, and overall geography should resemble Europe so the map feels familiar, but none of the countries, borders, capitals, or cities should use real-world names. Everything should use placeholder names that can be replaced later.

The game should focus on expansion, diplomacy, economics, military strategy, and world conquest while remaining easy to learn and fast-paced.

A full match should last 45-90 minutes.

Main Menu

When players join, they enter a lobby.

From the lobby they can:

Choose a nation.

View nation information.

Invite friends.

Customize cosmetics.

Vote for game settings.

Wait for enough players before the match starts.

Nation Selection

There are 51 playable nations spread across the continent.

Every nation occupies a unique location on the map.

Players select a nation before the match begins.

Each nation displays:

Placeholder Country Name

Flag (Placeholder)

Difficulty

Starting Economy

Population

Resources

National Bonus

Example:

Country 01

Capital:
Capital Alpha

Cities:

City Alpha

City Beta

City Gamma

City Delta

Country 02

Capital:
Capital Bravo

Cities:

City Echo

City Delta

City Sierra

City Omega

Every country should only use placeholder names until custom names are created later.

No real country names should appear anywhere.

Spawning

Once every player has selected a nation and the countdown ends:

Players automatically load into their nation's capital city.

The capital acts as the center of government.

Every capital contains:

Government Building

Barracks

Factory

Town Hall

Resource Storage

Spawn Point

Airport (locked early game)

Rail Station

Construction Yard

Players may freely walk around the capital while also controlling their nation through the strategy interface.

Map Design

The world is a fictional continent inspired by Europe.

The map should include:

Northern frozen regions

Western islands

Large mountain ranges

Central plains

Southern peninsulas

Eastern forests

Major rivers

Large lakes

Surrounding oceans

Although the terrain resembles Europe, every border is fictional.

No real borders should be copied exactly.

Provinces

Each nation contains several provinces.

Each province includes:

Population

Income

Infrastructure

Natural Resources

Defense

Happiness

Some provinces contain cities.

Others are farmland or wilderness.

Capturing provinces expands national territory.

Capitals

Every nation starts with exactly one capital.

The capital:

Produces the highest income.

Contains government buildings.

Acts as the nation's respawn point.

Stores national resources.

Can recruit every military unit.

If a capital is captured:

Production decreases.

National morale drops.

Income is reduced.

If the capital is recaptured, these penalties are removed.

Cities

Each nation contains multiple cities besides the capital.

City names are placeholders only.

Example city names:

City Alpha

City Bravo

City Charlie

City Delta

City Echo

City Foxtrot

City Gamma

City Nova

City Orion

City Zenith

These names are temporary and intended to be replaced during later development.

National Bonuses

Each nation begins with one randomly assigned or pre-designed bonus.

Examples include:

Industrial Nation

Military Tradition

Scientific Excellence

Trade Specialists

Agricultural Experts

Mining Efficiency

Engineering Experts

Economic Growth

These bonuses help make each nation feel unique.

Economy

Money is earned from:

Taxes

Cities

Factories

Trade

Resources

The player spends money on:

Buildings

Military

Technology

Infrastructure

Diplomacy

Espionage

Repairs

Resources

Resources generate automatically.

Types include:

Food

Steel

Oil

Coal

Stone

Wood

Gold

Rare Materials

Different provinces specialize in different resources.

Buildings

Players construct:

Factories

Research Centers

Military Bases

Farms

Power Plants

Harbors

Airfields

Hospitals

Police Stations

Fortresses

Buildings upgrade through multiple levels.

Higher levels greatly improve production.

Military

Military branches include:

Infantry

Mechanized Infantry

Heavy Infantry

Engineers

Tanks

Rocket Vehicles

Special Forces

Aircraft

Naval Fleets

Support Vehicles

Each unit has strengths and weaknesses.

Armies automatically fight when enemy forces meet.

Players influence battles using tactical abilities rather than controlling every soldier.

Diplomacy

Players may:

Declare War

Offer Peace

Create Alliances

Trade Resources

Share Intelligence

Guarantee Independence

Request Military Access

Send Financial Aid

Negotiate Treaties

Technology

Research categories:

Industry

Military

Construction

Agriculture

Medicine

Transportation

Communications

Energy

Only one technology may be researched at a time.

Completing research permanently improves the nation.

Public Happiness

Every nation tracks happiness.

High happiness provides:

Better income

Faster production

Higher recruitment

Greater stability

Low happiness causes:

Riots

Lower tax income

Reduced production

Possible rebellions

Victory Conditions

Players can win by:

Conquering the entire continent.

Owning the largest economy.

Completing all research.

Leading the strongest alliance.

Placeholder Naming Rules

During development:

Every country uses placeholder names.

Every capital uses placeholder names.

Every city uses placeholder names.

No real countries, capitals, regions, or city names should appear anywhere in the game until they are intentionally added later.

The map should clearly resemble Europe in its overall shape and geography, but all political entities, borders, and names should remain fictional and use temporary placeholders.

answers.ask: Should we build the whole continent as one strategic map, or one walkable capital city that every nation reuses?
answers.answer: Build the whole fictional Europe-inspired continent as one strategic map, with each nation having its own capital location. Capitals are walkable city areas where their owners spawn.

answers.ask: What era should the buildings and units read as - mid-century industrial, or contemporary?
answers.answer: Use a contemporary setting for buildings and units, matching the listed tanks, aircraft, mechanized forces, and modern infrastructure.

scene_prompt: Create a 3D multiplayer grand-strategy map of one fictional continent with a Europe-inspired overall land shape, surrounded by ocean. Lay out 51 uniquely positioned fictional nations with clearly distinct fictional borders, each divided into multiple provinces of cities, farmland, or wilderness; use placeholder country, capital, and city names only. Shape the terrain with frozen northern regions, western offshore islands, broad central plains, major mountain ranges, southern peninsulas, eastern forests, major rivers, and large lakes. Place one walkable contemporary capital city within each nation as its government center and player spawn, containing a government building, barracks, factory, town hall, resource storage, locked airport, rail station, construction yard, and surrounding urban streets. Distribute additional cities, industrial sites, farms, resource areas, harbors, airfields, and defensive structures across provinces according to terrain and coastlines.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy: territorial expansion, resource control, diplomacy, and army movement define the game.

## Shape and preset
Use `terrain-open` from the Real-Time Strategy preset. This is one contiguous continent where forces move dynamically across provinces rather than following fixed lanes.

## Config requirements
Apply `buildzone-plot` as broad national territory supporting distributed construction around each nation’s holdings. Draw `tracker-core` as each nation’s contemporary capital and governmental heart, with 51 such cores. Use `settlement-density` for the capital street grids and additional cities, `terrain-relief` for the major mountain ranges, `water-body` for the surrounding ocean, rivers, and large lakes, and `island-cluster` for the western offshore islands. The image must also show fictional borders and province divisions, frozen north, central plains, southern peninsulas, eastern forests, farmland, wilderness, industrial sites, farms, resource areas, harbors, airfields, and defenses.

## Layout requirements
Place `tracker-core` in both streams: site exactly one capital core inside each of the 51 national territories. Place 51 player spawn markers, one at each capital’s government center. Place `collectible-nodes` across suitable provinces, aligning food and timber with farms and forests and mineral resources with industrial terrain. Preserve distinct national and provincial ownership regions.

## Layout components
Build one huge Europe-shaped fictional continent bounded by ocean, partitioned into 51 nations and multiple provinces per nation. Each nation has one walkable capital urban zone containing a government building, barracks, factory, town hall, resource storage, airport, rail station, construction yard, and streets. Roads and rail connections link capitals, additional cities, farms, industrial and resource sites, harbors, airfields, and defensive positions. Frame the full continent from above with western islands and southern peninsulas legible against the ocean.

## Render order
Render `topdown` first and treat it as authoritative because 51 non-overlapping nations, their provinces, coastlines, and connected strategic geography must remain spatially coherent.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge, driven by the whole continent, 51 nations, and 51 walkable capitals. The theme is contemporary fictional geopolitical strategy. Use `tiered` for mountain relief and `CHECK` for ocean, rivers, lakes, and separated islands; no stacked surfaces, interiors, or separate maps require another modifier.
